entries.name: Ku-ring-gai Chase National Park

facts.claim: NPWS: Ku-ring-gai Chase National Park is always open but may close in poor weather or fire danger; West Head gates close 6pm to 6am (8:30pm to 6am in daylight saving).
NPWS park entry fee: $12 per vehicle per day (vehicles over 8 seats $4.40 per adult, $2.20 per child); a per-vehicle fee, not per person.
NPWS calls it Australia's second-oldest national park, in Sydney's north, with Bobbin Head picnic area, bushwalks, cycling, fishing and Aboriginal sites such as The Basin.
Live NPWS alerts (7-12 Oct 2026): Kalkari Lookout and Upper Gledhills Falls closed, Berowra walking track partly closed, 1080 fox baiting 1 Aug 2026 to 31 Jan 2027; no park-wide closure.

entries.name: Barrenjoey Lighthouse

facts.claim: NPWS: Barrenjoey Lighthouse, built 1881 from sandstone quarried on site, stands 91 m above sea level at Barrenjoey Head; no vehicle access (paid parking at Governor Phillip Park); about 30 minutes each way on Barrenjoey track (1 km) or the steeper Smugglers track; the inside is accessible only by guided tour but you can walk around the outside.
NPWS: park entry fees do not apply at this location.
NPWS guided tours generally run every Sunday at 11am, 12pm, 1pm, 2pm and 3pm (30 minutes); adult $15, concession $13, child $11, 10% discount for 4+; 1.1 km walk with steep sections.
NPWS local alerts for the lighthouse (reviewed 14 Oct 2026): no current alerts in the area.

entries.name: Penrith Whitewater Stadium

facts.claim: NSW Office of Sport (operator): built for the Sydney 2000 Olympics, a 320 m man-made river with Grade 3 whitewater rapids; whitewater rafting, kayak instruction, whitewater paddling and flatwater kayak hire; a new cafe (Sorelle) trades from 21 October 2026.

Guided rafting is from $135 per person (minimum age 12; raft, equipment, instruction and guide included; wetsuit hire $15); bookings are essential and rafting needs arrival 30 minutes before the start time.
Wikivoyage: at McCarthy's Lane, Cranebrook, the only man-made whitewater course of its kind in the Southern Hemisphere; rafting season noted as September to July.

entries.name: Audley

facts.claim: NPWS: Royal National Park is open 7am to 8:30pm; the Royal National Park Visitor Centre at 2 Lady Carrington Drive, Audley is open 8:30am to 4:30pm daily (closed Christmas Day).

NPWS: Audley Boatshed (operating since 1893) hires canoes, kayaks and rowboats on the Hacking River, 10am to 5pm Tuesday to Sunday (closed Monday unless a public holiday); Audley Dance Hall Cafe is nearby.

NPWS park entry fee: $12 per vehicle per day (vehicles over 8 seats $4.40 per adult, $2.20 per child); the fee is per vehicle, not per person, and does not apply to people arriving on foot or by ferry.

NPWS alert (reviewed 16 Oct 2026): some Royal National Park areas, including Wattamolla and Garie picnic areas, the Audley precinct trails and picnic flats, Garawarra Farm and Lady Carrington Drive, are closed between sunset and sunrise Monday to Thursday (excluding school holidays) from 6 July to 18 December 2026 for deer control.
NPWS alert: Varneys Bridge at Audley closed to vehicles 19 to 21 October 2026 (pedestrians allowed), cutting vehicle access to Wattle Forest and Currawong Flat picnic areas.

entries.name: Bundeena to Otford Coast Track

facts.claim: NPWS: The Coast Track is an iconic 27 km multi-day walk between Bundeena and Otford in Royal National Park, suggested over 2 days (Day 1 Bundeena to Garie Beach 17 km, at least 7 hours; Day 2 Garie to Otford 10 km, about 3 hours), Grade 4; park entry fees apply.

Overnight stays are at Garie Beach campground by advance booking only; humpback whale watching May to October; shorter sections can start at Bundeena, Wattamolla, Garie Beach, Garawarra Farm or Otford.
NPWS alert: coastal areas between Garie Beach and Figure 8 Pools and Garawarra Farm are closed sunset to sunrise Monday to Thursday (excluding school holidays) until 18 Dec 2026 (deer control).

entries.cost_note: NPWS vehicle entry fee applies only if you drive into the park ($12 per vehicle per day); walking in from Bundeena or Otford station does not pass a fee station.

entries.name: Wedding Cake Rock

facts.claim: NPWS: Wedding Cake Rock is very fragile and unstable and has a fence around it; stay behind the fenced areas (standing or sitting on the rock or cliff edges is a very high safety risk); allow at least 1 hour each way on a rough, steep, rocky track from Bundeena; the track is closed during total fire bans.

NPWS live alerts (reviewed 16 Oct 2026): no closure of the lookout or the track; only the night-time deer-control closure list (Mon-Thu, until 18 Dec 2026) and Skylight Cave (a separate nearby cave) permanently closed. Open for viewing from the fenced area.
Park entry fees apply if parking in Royal National Park ($12 per vehicle).

entries.hours: Daytime viewing (park open 7:00 AM – 8:30 PM); closed in total fire bans
entries.cost_note: NPWS vehicle entry fee applies only if you park in the park; walking from Bundeena does not pass a fee station. If you arrive on foot via Bundeena it is free.

entries.name: Yerranderie

facts.claim: NPWS: Yerranderie Regional Park protects a former silver-mining settlement turned ghost town; getting there means following 76 km of dirt road from Oberon; visitors walk the main street and historic buildings, take short bushwalks and visit the mine fields (a bridge crosses a large shaft); camping and cottages are bookable.

NPWS access: no access from Sydney's west through the Burragorang Valley (Sydney water catchment restrictions); access is via Oberon or Goulburn, over the Oberon-Colong stock route, and a low-range 4WD is required on the Jenolan-Kowmung route; not reachable by public transport.
Wikipedia: once a silver-mining town of about 2,000 people, mining collapsed in 1927; accessible mainly by a 4WD dirt road from Oberon (70 km); donated to NPWS by owner Valerie Lhuede.
NPWS alerts: Post Office Lodge closed for restoration until October 2027; fire ban for Kanangra Reserves from 1 Oct 2026.

entries.hours: Open daily; unsealed road, 4WD advised; check NPWS alerts
entries.cost_note: No park entry fee is listed on the NPWS page (accommodation and camping are bookable and priced separately).
